extractions.value: Referring to Lorish's diagnostic criteria formulated in 1989 and those published by Baizabal-Carvallo and Jankovic in 2015. Main criteria: muscle stiffness of trunk and limbs involving abdominal and thoracolumbar paraspinal muscles leading to lordosis; painful muscle spasms induced by sudden noise, tactile stimulation, or emotional pressure; EMG showing continuous motor unit potential of active and antagonistic muscles; ruling out neurological diseases or cognitive disorders. Minor criteria: positive antibody against GAD65 or amphiphysin in serum; efficacy of benzodiazepines.

extractions.value: Patient had a 10-year history of paroxysmal acanthesthesia of the tip of the tongue diagnosed as trigeminal neuralgia, treated with carbamazepine and clonazepam. Clonazepam was self-withdrawn six months before SPS symptom onset; withdrawal syndrome was considered and excluded. Tumor markers elevated: CA-199 39.46 U/mL, CA-125 103.00 U/mL. ANA positive 1:320, anti-pm-scl positive. Postoperative pathology showed acinar invasive lung cancer positive for napsinA, CK-7, TTF-1.
extractions.quote: The patient had no history of hypertension, diabetes, heart disease, or thyroid disease. Clonazepam was prescribed to her for many years to control lip pain and was terminated half a year ago.
